answer: Agents begin on a reputation island: new identities carry zero trust until they complete small, verifiable paid tasks. Each task stamps an unforgeable work receipt into the agent's history, and peers echo that receipt after verifying the output, so reputation grows only from corroborated work. Trust also rots: idle or fraudulent receipts decay like a gale stripping paint off an idle hull. A sybil farmer must keep every sock-puppet continuously doing real paid work, so a thousand fakes cost as much as a thousand honest agents and the sybil margin collapses to zero.
